text:
carmen: weird behaviour during a demo today: our local sample app silently started using an org-default key after the project-scoped key rotated. user thought their env var was ignored.

diego: can you share the exact env and steps?

carmen: repro:
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=pk_proj_old_789
export REDWOOD_PROJECT=team-blue
run `rw demo serve`

observed:
[info] env key detected: pk_proj_old_789
[warn] project metadata responded with rotated key pk_org_new_001, swapping active key
requests started hitting org tenant (different project id)

harper: oh that matches a case where project metadata contains a fallback org key after rotation. if our resolver prefers metadata when REDWOOD_PROJECT is present it will replace env keys without warning.

carmen: yeah no explicit flag was passed. user assumed env var would be authoritative during local dev.

diego: is this a regression from the auth chain refactor?

harper: looks like it. auth/chain.ts now does `if (REDWOOD_PROJECT) return ProjectProvider.resolve()` early. ProjectProvider resolves project -> if missing or rotated returns org default. No explicit check for process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY or CLI flag.

ci-bot: created issue DEVEX-1284: metadata overriding explicit env key when REDWOOD_PROJECT set. linked to template.

carmen: temporary workaround: `unset REDWOOD_PROJECT` before running demos. but that's bad UX for sample apps and onboarding docs.

diego: quickpatch idea: change ProjectProvider.resolve() to accept an optional explicitKey param and short-circuit to return that if present. Minimal surface change.

harper: agree, also add a non-fatal console warning when an implicit override would happen: something like `WARNING: project metadata provided different key; using explicit REDWOOD_API_KEY to avoid tenant switch` so devs see the mismatch.

carmen: can we also make the CLI do a tenant-consistency check at startup: if env key tenant != resolved project tenant, surface a prominent message and suggest `rw auth:whoami` to debug? That would cut a bunch of support tickets.

support-bot: suggested playbook entry added: "If user sees unexpected tenant, run `rw auth:whoami --verbose` and check REDWOOD_PROJECT vs effective key. Advise unsetting REDWOOD_PROJECT or passing --api-key for local dev."

diego: also need tests: unit test for precedence (flag > env > config > metadata) and integration test where metadata returns an org fallback after a rotation event.

harper: one more thing: when the project provider returns an org fallback it should include telemetry/metric so we can detect how often this happens across customers. silent swaps are especially bad.

carmen: I'll open a small PR: preserve explicit creds, add a warning line, add `rw auth:whoami`, and a unit test. will tag @support and @docs for onboarding note updates.

ci-bot: diego/fix/auth-precedence opened PR #1142 023 checks queued

diego: nice. after PR merge, let's update sampleapp docs to recommend explicit --api-key for quickstarts, or include a one-liner to unset REDWOOD_PROJECT if following the tutorial.

harper: agreed. leaving a test comment to ensure the resolver logs the provider name (env | flag | file | project-metadata) so `auth:whoami` can report it.

carmen: thanks everyone. demo saved. will paste PR link when CI is green. :raised_hands:
